normalization: Originals as fetched under original/: Internet Archive scans with their OCR layers, and the Project Gutenberg plain-text files as served. text/<slug>.ocr.txt is the Archive's OCR with line endings normalized; text/<slug>.txt is the Gutenberg file with line endings normalized. No text was corrected by hand by this seating. The Gutenberg transcription of the Principia is of the 1687 first edition; its transcribers record that they corrected a few typographical errors, listed at the end of the file. The Gutenberg Opticks is the fourth edition (1730), seated beside the first printing of 1704 as its clean text layer, the edition differing (the 1704 printing has sixteen Queries, the 1730 has thirty-one).
scope: Held: the Principia in its first edition of 1687, the scan with its OCR layer beside the Gutenberg transcription of the same edition; the Opticks in its first edition of 1704 (in English, with the two Latin mathematical treatises), the scan with its OCR layer, beside the Gutenberg transcription of the fourth edition of 1730. Noted and not seated: the second edition of the Principia (Cambridge, 1713, ed. Roger Cotes, with the General Scholium and 'Hypotheses non fingo'; Internet Archive bub_gb_SyNF4RBbkIgC, principiamathem00newtgoog) and the third (London, 1726, ed. Henry Pemberton; philosophinatur00cotegoog, A297190); the Latin Optice (1706). The Opticks of 1704 is English, so the seat is mul (Latin and English).

why_seated: The Principia joined the falling of bodies and the motions of the planets under one law of force, and the Opticks opened light into its colours by experiment. The seat holds both in their first printings, with the clean texts beside them, so that the first edition's Hypotheses and its sixteen Queries can be read before the later editions renamed and enlarged them.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-10-30: "and then an ea-corpora seating... Einstein, Gödel, Tesla, Copernicus, Galileo, classical Arabic mathematicians... what is in the public domain, and what else? and just to be perverse lets seat the promised Klee notebooks with them"; to the proposed set: "yes, thats a good set".
